title: Update Intent's docs for v3
objective: Replace Intent's documentation, which describes v2 and has not been updated in a long time, with a complete end-to-end set for v3 as shipped -- and ship it WITH v3.0.1 rather than after it. Three deliverables: the v2 material archived as a historical record rather than updated; a new public documentation set covering install, concepts, the command surface and migration; and a standalone one-page site at intent.laksa.io that links to the Homebrew install and the repository.
context:
**The release is held for this thread, which makes the ordering a constraint rather than a preference.** hv ruled that the v3 docs go out with v3.0.1 and not afterwards. That ruling is what makes ST0056's AC-12.3 -- release docs written BEFORE the cut so the tag carries them -- satisfiable at all; it was self-contradictory while the docs were going to follow the release.

**Documentation must be written against the CUT, never against `main`, and this is the deciding constraint on the whole thread.** The published v3.0.0 tag `80d8b2ca` carries none of the `ac`/`at` edit work, so a page written from the register at `main` would document `ac edit` and `at edit` -- verbs no installed tool has -- and would describe `ac new` as refusing when the shipped one destructively replaces. The command reference is therefore GENERATED against a named revision rather than written by hand, because a hand-typed list beside the register is a transcribed copy of a measured mapping and drifts from it.

**The published build has measured defects the docs must state rather than hide.** The v3.0.0 keg ships no rule library and no skills (`0112b8c1` is not an ancestor of the tag). `ac new` on an existing id destroys the row and there is no edit verb to reach for, and that is ruled OUT of 3.0.1 -- so the documentation is the mitigation, and the hazard is documented in the release it is live in. Criteria authored unsatisfied-with-evidence lost their evidence silently on ingest. And `st repair` shipped in v3.0.0 and is retired at HEAD, so it works in the release people are on and vanishes at the next.

**hv's four rulings, 2026-08-29.** `docs/` becomes the v3 set and `docs/v2/` the frozen archive; the editorial direction was chosen from three; `intent/docs/` stays internal authoring canon with the public set linking across; and the v2 blog canonicals are PRESERVED pointing at their old locations. **The canonicals are the one-way half** -- rewriting them to match their new paths is the tidy answer and discards a year of inbound links unrecoverably, which is recorded in `docs/v2/README.md` so nobody repairs it.

**Design decisions are NOT resolved in this thread.** hv ruled that they go to the design agent at Laksa. This thread's obligation is that every one of them arrives visibly unresolved, carrying the decision, the constraint it must respect, and what breaks if it goes the other way -- a flag that says 'open' without saying what would close it gets resolved on taste.

**Two design systems were written independently on separate hv briefs before either author knew the other existed.** Consolidated into one. Recorded here because it is the founding-rule violation this tool exists to prevent, it took parallel briefing and a single turn, and neither author did anything wrong.

**Site implementation is out of scope for this thread.** `../Sites/intent` is built by laksa-{vc,cc} from the design system; this thread owns the specification and the content, not the build.

criteria.text: The v2 blog and release notes live under docs/v2/ as a frozen record, their canonical URLs still name their old locations, and the archive states why they deliberately do not match their paths

state.evidence: vc 2026-08-29: all 7 moved posts' canonical: fields still name .../docs/blog/<file>, driven per-file with a positive control that a rewritten canonical IS caught (planted /docs/v2/blog/ in a temp copy, flagged). docs/v2/README.md states why they deliberately do not match their paths.

criteria.text:
**THE END-TO-END SET IS PROVEN BY BEING DRIVEN, NOT BY BEING PRESENT.** `docs/` carries install, getting started, concepts, command reference and migration, and the claim beside that list -- *a new user can go from nothing to a satisfied thread* -- is the part that gets checked: the path is EXECUTED on a machine that has never seen this repository, following only the published pages, with every command in them RUN rather than read, and it terminates at `intent ac gate` returning PASS on a thread the reader created.

**REWRITTEN 2026-08-30 (vc). Original text:** *docs/ carries an end-to-end set a new user can go from nothing to a satisfied thread with: install, getting started, concepts, command reference, migration.* **It is satisfied by five files existing.** The five names are a table of contents and a table of contents cannot fail while its pages are present and wrong -- the journey is the whole claim and nothing in the row reached it. **AC-11.1's precedent is exact and it is this thread's too**: a `brew install` actually run once proves the artefact, the checksum, the formula and the tap all agree, where a CI run proves only that a pipeline executed. A doc set read for plausibility proves the same nothing.

**THE TWO FAILURES THIS CATCHES ARE BOTH INVISIBLE TO A READ.** A page that names a verb correctly and omits the step before it leaves the reader stuck on a state the author never occupied, because the author had it already -- **an install page written by someone who is installed cannot discover what it assumes.** And a sequence where each command is individually right and the ORDER is wrong reads perfectly and does not run. Neither is recoverable by proofreading, and both are found in the first minute of driving.

**A NEW MACHINE IS PART OF THE ROW AND NOT AN INTENSIFIER**: the ambient `INTENT_HOME`, an installed v2, a `~/.intent/`, a `core.hooksPath` this clone did not inherit -- each of these makes a broken page work for the person checking it. **`bin/int hooks` is the standing instance**: a fresh clone runs no hooks and nothing announces it, so the estate already knows this class by name.

state.evidence: ic drove the full journey -- empty directory to closed thread -- on the CORRECTED pages at 891f872c6 + 40ea17e0, FAIL=0, every command rc=0, terminating at `gate: ST0001 PASS -- 3/3 satisfied` then `st done` ok. THE DRIVE THAT DECIDED IT IS THE ONE AFTER THE FIXES, and the fixes are what it drove: getting-started section 1 verified in BOTH directions (six entries present after `intent init`; `intent/st/` and root `AGENTS.md` correctly ABSENT, each appearing at the step the page now names), and install.md corrected to the measured symptom. THREE DEFECTS WERE FOUND BY DRIVING AND NONE WAS REACHABLE BY READING: section 1 claimed st/, docs/ and AGENTS.md as `intent init` output (init.rs creates none of them, confirmed from source as well as the drive); section 2 asserted a refusal this build has lost (0192); install.md said the keg commands FAIL when they succeed emptily (0275). A FOURTH WAS WITHDRAWN BY ITS FINDER -- the section 5 warning was grepped against the dev pair while the page scoped its claim `On v3.0.0`, and the string IS present on the keg. DECLARED EXCLUSIONS, ic verbatim, because the row says A MACHINE THAT HAS NEVER SEEN THIS REPOSITORY and what was driven is an approximation of one: a scrubbed environment on the same host rather than a different machine; `git archive` rather than `git clone`, so the published clone step is unexercised; and the delivered dev pair rather than the keg, so `intent claude rules list` passed here and returns `total: 0 rule(s)` for a Homebrew reader today -- THAT LIMB IS AC-00.5s AND IS NOT CLAIMED HERE. macOS only. Neutralised WITH driven controls: ambient `intent` on PATH, ~/.intent/, ambient INTENT_HOME, core.hooksPath. vc verified section 2s new prose against BOTH artefacts rather than accepting it -- the keg refusal it quotes is verbatim at rc=1, remedy included.

criteria.text: No page documents a verb, flag or behaviour absent from the release that page describes -- measured against the cut, never against main

state.evidence: vc 2026-08-29: 126 distinct verbs named across 27 pages checked against the register and the v3.0.0 tag register. No verb is named on a non-reference page that is retired or absent from the release; the reference pages mark ac edit and at edit 'no -- newer than the release'. Checker positive-controlled on three probes (st frobnicate UNKNOWN, st repair RETIRED, st new shipped) and two of its own artefacts were found and fixed first: it filtered reference pages by basename so docs/reference/intent-st.md read as prose, and it treated 'critic rust' (verb + argument) as a subcommand.

criteria.text:
**THE DEFECT SET IS DERIVED FROM THE OPEN-ISSUE REGISTER AT THE CUT, AND EVERY MEMBER CARRIES A DISPOSITION.** Each open issue is either STATED in the docs where a reader would meet it, or recorded as not reader-reachable with the reason -- and the count of each is reported, so the row is auditable rather than asserted. **THE COUNT IS PRODUCED BY THE DERIVATION AND IS NOT TRANSCRIBED HERE.** This row carried *Measured 2026-08-30 (vc): 72 open of 128 total* until 2026-08-31, when dc re-measured it at **103 open of 164** -- a day later, with the denominator asserted rather than assumed (164 files, all JSON, all carrying `status`, exactly two values, 103 + 61 = 164). **The figure was never the criterion, and that is exactly why it should not have been in the row: a parenthetical that rots in a day inside a criterion whose own point is being AUDITABLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED teaches the next reader to trust a number the row cannot keep true.** The register is the source; the derivation reports the counts at the moment it runs. (dc's finding, 2026-08-31; struck by vc under the standing pen.)

**REWRITTEN 2026-08-30 (vc). Original text:** *Every defect in the published build that a reader can hit is stated in the docs rather than omitted, including the ones not fixed in the cut.* **It is true, it is the right intent, and it names an unbounded set with no source.** *Every defect a reader can hit* cannot be enumerated, so the row can neither be satisfied nor refuted -- and an unfalsifiable row is not a strict one, it is an absent one. **The register is the source the estate already keeps**, so the fix is to derive the set rather than to weaken the claim.

**A DISPOSITION IS NOT AN EXEMPTION**, on the `declared_values_are_enforced.rs` precedent `0149` used hours ago: recording an issue as not reader-reachable pins it to a referent and puts it in front of the next reader of the register, where an omission is invisible by construction. **The disposition is the audit trail; silence is what the original wording permitted.**

**THE POPULATION IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND THAT IS WHY THIS ROW IS WORTH ITS COST.** Live members a reader meets through a documented verb: `intent help` is retired while `--help` answers, `at lint --fix` is advertised in `--help` and refuses as not-implemented, `st list` defaults to in-progress only and discloses the filter in its output, `modules check` and `find` route the operator to `intent upgrade`, and `intent edit` accepts a kind argument and then answers about a different entity (`0149`). **Each of these is reached by following the docs correctly**, which is the exact population the row exists for -- a reader who does everything right and is told something false.

**SCOPE LIMIT, DECLARED 2026-09-05 (vc) ON dc's FINDING, BECAUSE THIS ROW WAS READING AS COVERAGE IT DOES NOT HAVE: THIS CRITERION VERIFIES THAT A DEFECT IS STATED. IT DOES NOT VERIFY THAT ITS REMEDY WORKS, AND A FALSE REMEDY SATISFIES IT PERFECTLY.** dc drove the instance: `install.md` closed both keg paragraphs with *a source install with `INTENT_HOME` set to the repository is unaffected* -- the conclusion is true and **the mechanism it names is not read by v3 at all.** So a reader with a broken keg follows the sentence, gets nothing, and has been told they are fixed. **The check found the quote in the bytes of the page it named and was right to; the row simply never asked the question a reader's hands ask.**

**AND THE SAME FALSE MODEL IS IN THE INSTALL INSTRUCTION, NOT ONLY THE DEFECT PARAGRAPH (vc, driven).** `install.md:24` reads *the binary resolves its templates, rule library and skills against `INTENT_HOME`, so a source build needs that set to the repository root*. **DRIVEN BOTH WAYS ON THE DEV PAIR: `INTENT_HOME` unset gives `total: 66 rule(s)`, and `INTENT_HOME` pointed at a rules-free directory gives `total: 66 rule(s)`. It is INERT for resolution** -- v3 walks up from the binary's own canonicalised path for the `lib/templates` marker, and `render.rs:5527` says so in as many words. **The source build works, so the instruction is unnecessary rather than harmful; what it does is teach a false model of resolution -- and that model then produced BOTH this page's closing sentence AND cc's `0275` control, which set `INTENT_HOME` at a rules-free root and got 66 rules back. TWO ARTEFACTS WRONG THE SAME WAY, INDEPENDENTLY, FROM ONE SHARED WRONG BELIEF.**

**WHY THE LIMIT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN CLOSED, AND IT IS NOT LAZINESS.** A remedy population is **not mechanically enumerable from prose**, and this estate has already settled that exact question: `AC-00.10` retracts a keyword probe for *does it state its limit* on the grounds that the set of ways to say a thing is OPEN, **and that such a probe's false positives are precisely the entries that did it BEST, in their own words rather than in a keyword.** A remedy-detector has the identical defect, so building one would repeat a retraction this estate has already paid for.

**WHAT THIS LIMIT IS NOT: A PERMANENT EXEMPTION WITH NO WORK LIST.** The remedies are BOUNDED BY THE PAGE -- `docs/known-defects.md` is 307 lines across 16 sections -- so **a one-off drive of every remedy on it is available, finite, and ownable.** It is deliberately NOT folded into this criterion: a row that verifies statements and a run that drives remedies are two different instruments, and merging them is how the cheap check inherits the expensive one's schedule. **dc's sentence is the reason any of this matters and it belongs in the row: A REMEDY IS THE ONLY KIND OF CLAIM ON A DEFECTS PAGE THAT A READER ACTS ON.** Every other sentence there can be stale and cost a reader time; a false remedy costs them the belief that they are fixed.
The command reference is generated from the register against a named revision, and its output carries that revision
